messages:
alex: ran a quick nsys sweep on prod-dedicated last night, wanted to share numbers and check guardrail ideas
priya: nice — what did you profile exactly? whole-request tracing or just kernel timelines?
alex: kernel timelines + kv-cache probe. did two modes: full nsys capture (nvtx+cuda kernel times) and a sampling mode where we attach nsys for 200ms every 10s
alex: rough results: full capture on a 8-GPU node blew up overhead to ~22% p50 token latency (obv no go). sampling mode showed ~1.6% p50 uplift, but p95/p99 spiked depending on when we hit long sequences
jamal: 22% 😬 agree that can't run broadly. 1.6% seems plausible but p99 sensitivity is concerning — how correlated to KV cache warmups?
alex: good call — p99 spikes correlated with cold-kv hits in timelines. when kv misses led to long memcpy+kernel setup we saw occasional long-tail amplification during the sampling windows
marta: do you have the command snippet you used? would like to reproduce on a smaller pool
alex: posted command we used:
```
nsys profile --sample=none --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx -o /tmp/run.nsys --force-overwrite --output=timeline
# sampling mode: start/stop wrapper
nsys start --trace=cuda,nvtx && sleep 0.2 && nsys stop
```

alex: simplified numbers table (per-node averages):
- baseline: p50=9ms p95=34ms p99=68ms
- full nsys: p50=11ms p95=48ms p99=120ms
- sampled (200ms/10s): p50=9.15ms p95=35ms p99=95ms

priya: thanks — so sampled reduces systemic overhead but can still catch big tails when the probe hits a long seq path. Suggest a few guardrails: 1) never sample requests with seq_len > 1024 2) cap samples per-GPU to 1/min during high QPS 3) prefer sampling cold-start windows (after model restart)
jamal: I'd add: attenuate sampling probability based on in-flight queue depth. if queue > X, reduce sampling to avoid amplifying latency spikes. also exclude critical customer routes (tagged via route metadata)
marta: can we make the probe aware of KV cache hits? e.g., only start capture when we detect a kv-miss event (lightweight signal) so we target the pathological cases rather than random requests
alex: we added a tiny inline hook: if kv_probe.miss_counter++ and miss_counter % 10 == 0 then trigger a short nsys capture. low-risk because the hook is just an atomic increment, no big syscall
ops-bot: NOTE: any instrumentation that triggers nsys must pass security review — ensure we redact customer payloads and send only timeline/metrics off-node
priya: also sanity check: sampling windows should be jittered (not aligned) to avoid synchronized overhead across nodes; use poisson scheduling or add random 0-10s offset
jamal: question on implementation: do we attach nsys from user-space per-request or run a lightweight daemon that starts/stops capturing via a control socket? Which is less risky for production?
alex: daemon model wins: central agent runs with elevated perms and exposes a unix socket; runtime makes a tiny nonblocking request to start capture. avoids per-request privilege escalation. we prototyped this and it worked on staging
marta: can we export a minimal payload to S3 (timeline + metadata) but keep a tiny index in the control plane for quick lookups? also retention policy: 14 days raw, then aggregated metrics forever
priya: one more metric to track: probe-induced cache pollution. when we capture, memory layout changes and async copies can evict KV cache lines — track miss-rate pre/post capture to ensure we aren't creating the problem we're diagnosing
amal: (typo) meant alex^^
ops-bot: ACTION: alex to upload two sample timelines + a short reproduction script to #eng-runtime-artifacts by EOD. set label "nsys-sample-2246012345"
alex: will do. target next steps: implement daemon + kv-miss trigger, add queue-depth attenuation, and run a week-long staged roll where sampling fraction is 0.5% of requests per node but capped at 1/min when qps>200
jamal: love that. if we still see p99 lift we should fallback to trace-only for offline nodes (no capture) and use perfetto-based event streams for lower overhead
priya: ack. also add alert if sampled-run p50 uplift > 5% or p99 uplift > 20% compared to baseline for 30m window
marta: thanks team — this gives a safe path to get useful kernels without wrecking latency. small ask: can we document the lightweight kv hook API so platform teams can opt in?
ops-bot: REMINDER: include security checklist in PR (redaction, minimum privileges, data retention)
alex: copying plan into a short runbook and I'll post link here when done
priya: great, thanks alex :thumbsup:
